answer: Stone dust coats the yard, and the mason squares the block with a few sure strokes. Proof of stonemason arch via keystone wedge count — an arch the mason wedges only after 31 arches run true, each arch keystoned by the mason himself. The mirror is the scaffold the arch is raised from. The ember is the level the courses are checked with. The voyage is the yard where the cut stone waits. A forger must match the wedge line by line, 31 lines in all, and the last line still gives him away.
